behaviors.title: Native image paste and errors
assertions: Mixed format PNG and TIFF paste uses image bytes on the target host
Pasted path and following input arrive as separate arguments
Oversized and capability-limited image paste show errors and leave a usable terminal
Ctrl-V in a plain shell reaches the raw PTY unchanged
A refused storage directory leaves its occupant and shell intact

behaviors.title: Pending workspace and worktree operations
assertions: Failed worktree creation preserves existing state and supports explicit Retry or Dismiss
Successful Retry creates one usable workspace
A real blocked Git checkout is pending until released, then exposes a usable first terminal
Opening the same local or remote directory twice leaves one live workspace at that path
Completing a worktree does not take back selection after the user moves away
Local New Workspace starts a usable terminal in the private home
Workspace order stays fixed during a pending checkout and can change after completion
Opening an existing checkout gives one terminal in the selected checkout, including the exact remote branch and working directory
During a pending worktree handoff the previous terminal receives no key input and remains usable after reselecting it

behaviors.title: Creation interruption and compatibility
assertions: Capability-limited remote fallback creates a live terminal using the peer home
Explicit Retry after a real timed-out operation results in one workspace
Cutting the client SSH path leaves the peer's checkout running, and Retry recovers its one persisted workspace
Retry after a remote daemon restart selects the persisted checkout if present and does not resubmit an unconfirmed checkout

behaviors.title: Explicit server takeover and rollback
assertions: Cancel preserves the existing server and its session identities
Confirm uses the current build with the same workspace layout and new sessions
A newer server offers only a client upgrade and leaves the remote sessions intact
A signed replacement refused by the real remote service rolls back to the prior server and saved layout
An actual interrupted installation remains pending until recovery is confirmed, then restores the previous build and layout without replay
Confirmation is bound to the inspected process; a stale confirmation makes no change, and Retry prepares fresh consent
A foreign local daemon can be replaced after confirmation, with the saved workspace and one execution of each command

behaviors.title: Timeout diagnostics and server operations
assertions: A stopped owned daemon exposes Retry and resumes without replacing the daemon or shell
SSH transport failure exposes inspection and Retry while disabling destructive actions and preserving the remote server
Offline or rejected SSH reports an unavailable server, and the retry action preserves the peer
An unavailable status remains legible in the workspace outline and machine list at narrow window sizes

behaviors.title: Nested settings update flows
assertions: An available managed update prepares a sheet from Settings and cancellation preserves the installation
A newer server offers an app upgrade instead of server replacement
A slow signed download shows progress with install disabled and cancellation preserves state
A foreign server is presented as a takeover confirmation before applying an app upgrade
Settings presents exactly one native upgrade or recovery sheet and retains the surrounding Settings controls after cancellation
Unmanaged installations show the checked release in Settings with upgrade disabled and no updater notice in the main window
Missing the minimum client release leaves the remote server and shells intact without enabling an app upgrade
A skipped release can still be staged explicitly in Settings

behaviors.title: Account grouping and source availability
assertions: A configured account is visible without any active agent session
Shared logins collapse to one page, separate logins can be selected independently
A remote-only account shows last known usage while disconnected and clears its stale warning on reconnect
Organizations that share a login email remain distinct from each other and other providers
Disabling a provider in Settings hides its cards while preserving other provider usage and terminal input
The merged account adds active provider processes across both machines
A rejected remote login has its own sign-in state and no local Keychain action, while the local login remains usable
Missing account identity stays on its own page and authentication and rate-limit failures remain visible

behaviors.title: Reported agent identity and lifetime
assertions: Canonical provider and reported source appear via the public CLI and visible pane label
Acknowledgement/clear retain provider; shell return ends it
Titles alone do not register agents
Foreground acknowledgement preserves reported provider identity
Client relaunch preserves live identity and a daemon restart clears it from the new shell
Registered coordinator provider and role appear on its pane and in the visible terminal header

behaviors.title: Focus acknowledgement and close confirmations
assertions: Closing an exited workspace requires no confirmation and preserves its files
Completion stays unread on an inactive tab and selecting it acknowledges only its activity
Terminal focus returns after inline editing without an extra focus click
A live worktree or coordinator requires confirmation before closing its otherwise empty project
An inactive client leaves completion unread; reselecting the workspace in the active client acknowledges that pane
An empty project and worktree close as a group without a confirmation or checkout removal
Pending workspace selection keeps terminal input away from the previous pane

behaviors.title: Synchronized frames, cursor and sidebar presentation
assertions: Native pixel samples during a fragmented redraw show the last completed frame
An unterminated redraw eventually publishes its frame and terminal input continues
The renamed editor shows its new text without the old label in native pixels
Hidden, steady and blinking cursor states are distinguishable in actual native terminal pixels
Long Unicode titles remain accessible and survive resize and client relaunch
The actual terminal remains legible across light and dark appearance and resize
The inset sidebar leaves both copies of the machine status readable beside a long name
